issues.summary: The HD3 and HD4 notes say 'AKI - worsening, Cr trending up, nephrology consulted, renal US ordered'. This contradicts Cr 0.9 on the same notes, the HD2 note saying AKI resolved, and the discharge summary. It looks like stale copy-forward text. No nephrology note exists, and no AKI recurrence or ATN is coded.

AKI and dehydration due to norovirus gastroenteritis were both present on admission. Sequencing the AKI as principal follows the attending's discharge summary. The gastroenteritis (A08.11) is the underlying cause and is a reasonable alternative principal diagnosis. Confirm the sequencing choice.

Low bicarbonate (HCO3 19) was found on admission labs without a documented diagnosis. Consider querying for acidosis. Also consider querying whether the AKI was ATN, since the creatinine recovered quickly, which suggests it was not.

The HD3 and HD4 notes carry identical 'AKI - worsening, Cr trending up, nephrology consulted, renal US ordered' text despite Cr 0.9 and no nephrology note or renal US result. Ask the provider to clarify or amend so the AKI is not read as persistent or worsening. The same note also says to restart losartan, which is inconsistent with ongoing worsening AKI.

The AKI diagnosis rests on Cr 2.1 vs baseline 0.9 (about 2.3x) with recovery to 0.9 within about 24h of fluids. This meets KDIGO, but a payer may challenge it as dehydration with prerenal azotemia. The record should explicitly support the AKI criteria. The coder's issues list did not flag this.

The near-fall and generalized weakness are symptoms and are likely integral or covered by the unsteady gait and deconditioning documentation. Avoid separate coding of weakness. A history-of-falls or fall-risk code is not clearly supported by the documentation.
